sections.overview: The shortfin spiny eel is a deep-water member of the notacanth family, despite its eel-like outline.
sections.identification: It has an elongated body and separate dorsal spines; the accepted name is Notacanthus bonaparte, though many older papers use N. bonapartei.
sections.habitat: Records place it on deep continental slopes in the eastern North Atlantic and Mediterranean, often from several hundred to about two thousand metres.
sections.diet: Mediterranean stomach analyses found a benthic diet including echinoderms and sessile animals such as anemones and bamboo-coral polyps.
sections.behavior: In the Balearic Sea it was most abundant over the middle slope, and larger fish occurred deeper than smaller ones.
sections.reproduction: A Mediterranean study found reproduction from late summer into autumn and suggested adults move deeper when breeding.
sections.ecology: Its specialized benthic feeding links the fish to deep-sea communities, including habitat formed by the bamboo coral Isidella elongata.
sections.conservation: Deep-water trawl surveys have caught the species at depths used by commercial fisheries, but the studies cited here do not establish a global population trend.
